source_snapshot.title: feat(agent): unify Ix context, provenance, and investigation workflows for agents
source_snapshot.body:
## Summary

Agents investigating a target currently stitch together many disconnected
graph/evidence results by hand. This PR adds a bounded, deterministic context
bundle — `ix context <target>` — that composes Ix's existing intelligence into
one coherent, provenance-aware answer, and exposes it over CLI and MCP
(`ix_context`).

## Existing Ix context/provenance infrastructure

Ix already ships a rich graph surface that this PR composes rather than
replaces: entity/claims/edges (`ix entity`), conflicts (`ix conflicts`),
history, impact, trace, rank, stale detection, decisions, and the `/v1/context`
service that returns claims/conflicts/decisions/intents for a seed.
`--format llm` gives a token-minimal wire format. The new command is genuine
compositional work on top of those services — it does not create a second
context engine, a second graph model, or a parallel ranking engine.

## Problem

- Agents get fragments: one call for claims, another for edges, another for
  history, another for staleness — each with its own ordering and shape.
- No bounded output: nothing stops a wide target from flooding the context.
- No explicit truncation: silent trimming hides what was dropped.

## New context composition

`ix context <target>` produces an `ix-context-bundle/1` schema object with:

- `target` — resolved id/name/kind and resolution mode.
- `entities` — target plus referenced nodes, deduped and ordered
  deterministically (kind, name, id).
- `relationships` — graph edges, ordered deterministically (src, dst,
  predicate).
- `claims`, `decisions`, `conflicts`, `intents` — straight from the existing
  context service, preserving their shapes.
- `provenance` — source URI/hash, extractor, source type, observedAt,
  introduced rev, history length, staleness.
- `freshness` — `current` / `stale` / `unverified`, never silently presenting
  historical evidence as current.
- `evidence` — ranked items with `score`, `kind`, `reason`, `refs`.

## Determinism

For identical repository state, scope, target, options and budgets, the bundle
is byte-stable apart from the single declared time-dependent field
(`generatedAt`). Ordering is fixed at every level: entities by kind/name/id,
relationships by src/dst/predicate, evidence by a deterministic relevance tier
then a stable id tiebreaker. Nothing depends on hash order, insertion order,
or iteration order.

## Context bounds

Every budget is explicit and clamped:

- `--max-entities` (default 50, max 500)
- `--max-relationships` (default 100, max 1000)
- `--max-evidence` (default 25, max 200)
- `--max-chars` (default 12000, max 1_000_000)

When reduction occurs the bundle reports `truncation` — entitiesTruncated,
relationshipsTruncated, evidenceTruncated, charactersTruncated — so the caller
always knows what was dropped and can rerun with larger budgets.

## Evidence ranking

Ranking is deterministic-tier based: target (0), direct structural facts from
the shared explain collector (10+), context claims (20), decisions (21),
conflicts (22), intents (23), graph relationships (30+), provenance (40), with
a stable id tiebreaker. It reuses the existing facts collector and context
service — no second ranking engine.

## Provenance

Provenance comes from the existing `/v1/provenance` service and the explain
facts collector. Nothing is fabricated; unverified fields stay absent.

## Freshness

Staleness comes from the shared facts collector (`facts.stale`), which is the
same signal `ix explain` uses. A stale bundle is flagged in `freshness` and
warned on in text output; classification is `stale` when the source changed
since last ingest, `current` otherwise.

## Investigation state, resume, deltas

Resumable investigation state and deltas are the explicit next tranche of this
branch. The context bundle already gives every resumed run a stable, comparable
starting point: schema-versioned, deterministic, budgeted, with explicit
truncation — so a state file keyed by a stable investigation id can store
explored entities, evidence, claims, unresolved questions and the last context
generation, and a resumed run replays only the delta. The schema is stable
precisely so that delta comparison is meaningful.

## MCP / CLI

- CLI: `ix context <target>` with `--kind`, `--path`, `--pick`, `--depth`,
  `--as-of-rev`, `--max-*`, `--format text|json|llm`.
- MCP: `ix_context` tool with `target`, `as_of_rev`, `max_entities`,
  `max_relationships`, `max_evidence` arguments, returning the JSON bundle.
- Both share one implementation and one schema.

## Export

The JSON bundle is the portable representation: stable IDs, provenance,
revisions, evidence kinds, relationships, freshness, verification. It has no
dependency on Ix-findings paths, generated HTML, or findings-specific imports.

## Testing

- Determinism: identical input twice ⇒ identical static output (only
  `generatedAt` differs).
- Budgets: `maxEntities: 1` ⇒ exactly one entity + positive
  `entitiesTruncated`; `maxRelationships: 0` ⇒ zero relationships + positive
  truncation; evidence capped by count.
- Freshness: `stale: true` facts ⇒ `{ stale: true, classification: "stale" }`.
- Evidence ordering: scores ascending, target first, structural above claims.
- MCP: `ix_context` registered and served; context tests 4/4, MCP suite 15/15,
  typecheck clean.

## Historical links

Earlier MCP implementation and hardening work in the `Alot1z/Ix-remap`
development fork:

- https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/36c7c7eccd8068d48df4f61394b42a3ffa62483c — `feat(mcp): add ix mcp subcommand exposing the code graph as MCP tools (#219)`
- https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/66111917a2a58437c91372616f98928876121395 — `fix(mcp): abort in-flight calls on EOF, add ix_read tool, executor timeout coverage`
- https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/1a5b0b93c9e8871610370c0f36212be8f6cf6980 — `fix(mcp): harden the stdio server — line-size cap, tree-kill, protocol-abuse matrix (#219)`

## Ix-findings evidence

- MCP overview: https://alot1z.github.io/Ix-findings/mcp/
- MCP architecture: https://alot1z.github.io/Ix-findings/mcp/implementation/
- MCP security: https://alot1z.github.io/Ix-findings/mcp/security/
- Original issue #219: https://alot1z.github.io/Ix-findings/issues/219/

## Relationship to PR1

PR1 (#422, `feat(mcp): enrich Ix MCP tools with structured outputs, semantic
annotations, and stronger agent interoperability`) gives the shared MCP surface
typed structured results and truthful annotations. PR2 builds the bounded
context layer on the same surface. PR1's annotations tell agents which calls
are safe to repeat; PR2's bundles give agents the answer in one bounded call.
They are independent branches against `main`.

commits.message:
feat(context): deterministic bounded context bundles via `ix context`

Compose the existing resolver, fact collector, and /v1/context service
into a single deterministic, budgeted context bundle with explicit
truncation metadata and provenance. Evidence is ranked by a stable
tier order (target, structural, claim, decision, conflict, intent,
relationship, provenance) with an id tiebreaker, so identical input
produces identical output apart from the declared generatedAt field.

Adds the `ix context <target>` command with text/json/llm formats,
--max-* budgets, --as-of-rev historical context, and staleness
classification from collected facts.

feat(context): expose ix_context over MCP and support JSON export

Add the ix_context MCP tool with bounded budget parameters
(--max-entities/--max-relationships/--max-evidence) and optional
historical --as-of-rev, wired through the same argv isolation and
json formatting as the other JSON-backed tools. The context command
also gains --out <path> to write the bundle to a file, so evidence
bundles can be exported for review or storage.

The MCP catalog now lists ix_context for OSS installs; Pro-only
tool gating is unchanged.
